text:
Sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons: [Hidasi and Czapp, 2023](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf) show substantial disagreements between full-catalog evaluation and ranking against 100 sampled negatives; popularity sampling does not reliably recover true ranks. [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) evaluates sampling reliability through Kendall rank agreement and exposure-bias robustness. Thus, improved sampled diagnostics should not be assumed to imply improved full-catalog retrieval.

Popularity-stratified analysis is particularly relevant: [Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) find that aggregate sequential-recommendation metrics hide head/mid/tail imbalances; random-negative training favors head items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance at an overall accuracy cost. Proposed diagnostic application: replace raw score margins with positive rank, reciprocal rank, and pairwise win rate; stratify by history length, training-item frequency, and negative difficulty. Add frequency-matched negatives and same-model high-scoring unseen negatives as supplementary probes. Compare original versus shuffled-history ranks to assess dependence on sequence order; [RecSys 2024 work](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential/) uses shuffling to investigate sequential structure. These probes indicate sensitivity, not causal proof of useful sequence learning.

For uncertainty, [evaluation-methodology research](https://evazangerle.at/publication/bauer-dagstuhl-2024/bauer-dagstuhl-2024.pdf) recommends quantifying variability across users. Proposed application: paired user-level bootstrap within each category, recomputing the four-category macro HR@10 difference and reporting 95% intervals and stratum counts. Keep candidate sets fixed across comparisons. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the trained models and candidates, not training randomness or repeated-search bias. Retain the pinned validation HR@10 as the selection objective; use diagnostic agreement and full-catalog ranks only as supplementary evidence, without fitting another predictor.
